summary.intent: Build, at START Hack Munich (Lio challenge 'Keep the Line Running'), a general supply-chain launch-control product that rechecks Soony's launch plan against documents, finds contradictions, and acts (supplier emails, calls, routines) with human approval for money and plan changes.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found the Collector's Edition and game cards short despite an 'all ok' plan, then built a polling pipeline and a web app (Today decisions, Launch overview, Routines, Suppliers, voice two-step confirmation). Generalized the delivery site and cutoff naming; the latest Launch/Today split was built and reviewed, with 10+ commits still unpushed.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks; the documented way to detect changes is polling with SHA-256 comparison, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/; .env holds the token and .env.example is committed with an empty value.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no repo changes log 'skipping checkpoint'.
The server runs uvicorn without reload, so backend changes (e.g. new launch.parts data) need a restart to show in the live app; web/dist is served by FastAPI.
Spreadsheets are recognised by columns rather than file names, and supplier documents are read by a model, but a file with renamed columns is skipped silently, which is a gap to warn about.
Plan page was replaced by Launch (/launch); Today holds all decisions and case groups, and /plan redirects to /launch.
Soony-specific wording ('trucks', 'Hamburg') leaked into code; delivery site now comes from sites.csv and the cutoff name should be configurable per customer.
Voice decisions now need prepare_decision then decide with a one-time token (TOKEN_TTL_S=600), stored in voice_tokens.json; the browser also guards decide behind a user utterance.

code.finding: prepare_decision returns a summary and one-time token; decide requires token and confirmed, preventing the model from acting without a spoken yes.
New module providing the launch field in build_state(): per-part run-dry times, hours left and shipment state joined from open_shipments.csv, from the verifier's dispatch.json.
Verifier originally ignored arrivals (34,800 game-card gap); fixed, and a fallback key was added because the reader put the part number in `item`, giving the real 6,800 gap.

workflow: Data findings showed the plan said 'ok' while documents showed overbooked art book receipts (80,000 vs 8,000), a failed statue lot, and mismatched sleeve revisions; a subagent cross-check of all OCs and scans was effective.
Parallel builder subagents on overlapping files (Today.tsx, api.py) risk conflicting edits; handing work off via SendMessage and checking commits afterward worked.
Tests that called decide directly had to be updated to the two-step flow after adding a safety requirement.
Never approve or accept on real data in tests, since it sends real supplier emails.

friction: Token was initially empty in .env, blocking data access until the user supplied it.
User repeatedly rejected cluttered, unprofessional UIs and redundant views (Flow/Steps/Expanded, Today vs Plan overlap), costing several iterations.
Voice assistant announced it would outline actions then proceeded straight to 'Done', requiring a safety redesign.
The live server needed manual restarts to expose new backend data, so the Launch page showed 'unknown' until then.
Concurrent edits to api.py by multiple agents created confusion about whose changes were whose.
Voice flow could not be tested end to end because there was no mic available.
open_items: Push the 10+ local commits on jonas/today-flow (requires explicit user approval).
Run a live voice call to verify the two-step decision flow end to end.
Build the data-shape check that warns when file columns change or unknown file types appear, with an 'Ask Nils (IT)' action, then show it on Launch.
Make the cutoff label ('trucks') a per-customer setting in the UI.
Write the README, demo script, video (max 3 min) and deck for the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
Register sender email addresses in the portal and actually send the Karton Nowak art-book order and the Boise reply.
Decide PR handling (#5 vs jonas/today-flow into main).
Emails edited on screen and then confirmed by voice currently send the original draft, since decide takes no text.
Decide whether to delete the older Claude doc after the briefing page was published.
